files.review: Read all 842 original lines and the complete actual designAgent factory plus queue and tool owners. Replaced HTTP 400 request-shape probes with complete successful Responses SSE decoded by the installed OpenAI provider and native ToolLoopAgent. Four actual phases retain identical tool grammar, stateless encrypted-reasoning/cache options and strict-mode registration. Native required-question call covers the bounded first five of seven. Native concurrent provider calls prove that a client question or server wait terminal respects an earlier unfinished catalog callback and refuses a later decoded call. Controlled Project inspection is explicitly an ordering boundary, not a Project authorization claim. Removed duplicated direct-tool identity predicate cases with root approval; native PostgreSQL staging and provider-schema parsing owners cover those invariants.

Read all 67 original lines. Removed the fabricated double-cast ModelMessage checkpoint and callback-spy projection tests. A complete real Responses checkpoint followed by two native registered tool calls and final text now proves the installed SDK decoder preserves opaque id/encrypted bytes, drops the pre-checkpoint prefix, retains both function-call/output pairs, and includes exactly one fresh server packet across three actual provider requests.

Separated ten pure authorization cases from transport coverage using typed UI cards parsed by the actual askQuestions schema. Checks stable wire grammar versus exact prose admission, localized candidate labels, first-five bounded authorization across two rounds, pending-set reordering, identity and related-scope changes, six forged or incomplete card variations, partial answer progress and retention beside a later unanswered card. Removed incidental serialized authorization length assertion.

New migrated PostgreSQL coverage binds a native Responses checkpoint to actual started/completed context records and usage, appends a real convertToModelMessages user continuation, and reopens the durable context. Forged state heading and a copied genuine pre-checkpoint server packet both reproduced missing fresh state before the source fix. After the fix, both require a fresh authoritative packet persisted after the boundary and preserve completed response identity. A real PostgreSQL lock proves packet commit precedes the next provider request; another reopen proves durable-origin reuse avoids duplicate state. This tests actual factory/store composition and does not claim the full design runner executed. Typecheck follow-up removed an excess conversion-input id and replaced nonexistent completedSteps.messages comparisons with nonempty exact persisted response-item and completed-usage-identity equality.
